text:
A: Hello? Ah, there we are. Sorry, sorry, I've been sat here clicking the wrong button for about a minute. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yeah, I can hear you fine. Don't worry, I only just got on myself really.
A: Oh, that's kind of you to say. I'm Graham, er, Newark, Nottinghamshire way.
B: I'm Joanne. I'm in Taunton, Somerset.
A: Taunton, lovely. We've driven through Taunton, I think, on the way to somewhere. Devon probably.
B: Yeah, that's what most people do, to be fair. They just drive through.
A: Did you do that puzzle thing at the start? I'll be honest, I sort of got about halfway and then I think I just guessed.
B: Oh God, yeah. Erm, I was fine at first and then the last couple I was just staring at it. I'm not a puzzle person really. I do Wordle and that's about my limit, you know?
A: My wife does Wordle. Linda. Every morning, and she tells me her score whether I've asked or not.
B: That's me with my daughter. What do you do, Graham, if you don't mind me asking? Are you retired?
A: Er, no, well, I keep meaning to be. I'm a solicitor. Small firm on the high street, wills, probate, a bit of house buying and selling. I'm senior partner, which sounds very grand, but really it means I couldn't get out of it fast enough when the old boy retired. And I've been saying I'll go down to three days for about five years now, and my secretary Janet just sort of rolls her eyes at me.
B: Oh, bless her. I bet she runs the place really.
A: She does, she absolutely does. I lose a file, she finds it. Er, where was I... oh, what about yourself?
B: Erm, I'm a team leader at an insurance call centre. Home insurance. I've got eleven on my team and I still take the escalated calls, the ones where people are, you know, really upset. Flood claims and that.
A: Oh, that must be hard going.
B: It can be. But honestly, most of the time people just want someone to actually listen to them. Once you let them get it all out, they calm down.
A: That's very true. That's half of what I do, really. Somebody's lost their mum, and they come in and they're worried about the forms, but it's not the forms, is it.
B: No. No, it's not. Sorry, that's... yeah. My dad died four years ago, and I remember the solicitor being really kind, and it made such a difference.
A: I'm sorry, duck. That's a hard thing.
B: Thank you. It's fine. Anyway! Sorry. Do you get holidays and that, or are you always working?
A: Oh, we go to the same bit of the Norfolk coast every summer. Thirty years. Same pub, same fish and chips.
B: That's me with Cornwall! Static caravan, same week every year, near St Ives. The kids moan, but they love it really.
A: Ours used to moan. Now they've got kids of their own who moan. Funny how it goes round.
B: Is that a dog I can hear? Oh no, sorry, that's mine. Pip. She's snoring under the table.
A: Oh, lovely. We had a Labrador, but he went two years ago. Linda says no more, but I keep looking at them in the park.
B: Aw. You'll crack.
A: I probably will. I'll tell her it was her idea.
B: That's exactly how I got Pip, except it was my ex-husband's idea and now she's mine.
A: Ha. Possession is nine tenths, as they say. Professionally I can't comment.
B: What do you do outside work, then?
